```{r data, include=FALSE}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD DATA ONCE

input <- '.'

#### OCEAN THRESHOLD ####
grids_thresholds <- st_read(file.path(input, 'Data/data/1_preprocessing/atlas-grids/grids-ocean-thresholds/grids_ocean_thresholds.shp'))
thresholds <- grids_thresholds$kvdrtkd[grids_thresholds$pct_lnd >= 25]

#### EFFORT ####
get_effort <- function(dir){
  atlas1 <- read_excel(file.path(dir, 'effort', 'dækning atlas1+2.xlsx'), sheet = 'kvadrater atlas1')
  atlas2 <- read_excel(file.path(dir, 'effort', 'dækning atlas1+2.xlsx'), sheet = 'kvadrater atlas2')
  
  atlas2 <- atlas2 %>% 
    select(-UNDS_KODE_) %>% 
    rename(UNDS_KODE_ = UNDS_KOD_1)
  
  # Load design (Note: 'design' object is overwritten here in original code)
  load('HmscOutputs/2026-02-10_07-03-53_All_All_Atlas3_MinOccs5/Models/Fitted/HPC_samples_0250_thin_100_chains_4.Rdata')
  design <- read.csv('Data/data/1_preprocessing/design/studyDesign.csv')
  xycoords <- design[design$atlas == 2, c('site', 'lat', 'lon')]
  
  key <- read_excel(file.path(dir, 'effort', 'dækning atlas1+2.xlsx'), sheet = 'dækning') %>% 
    mutate(coverage = case_when(
      UNDSKODE == 0 ~ 'Not understood',
      UNDSKODE == 1 ~ 'Good',
      UNDSKODE == 2 ~ 'Average',
      UNDSKODE == 3 ~ 'Bad'
    ))
  
  effort <- rbind(
    atlas1 %>% mutate(atlas = 1),
    atlas2 %>% mutate(atlas = 2)
  ) %>% 
    left_join(key %>% rename(UNDS_KODE_ = UNDSKODE), by = "UNDS_KODE_") %>% 
    rename(site = KVADRATKOD) %>% 
    left_join(xycoords, by = 'site')
  
  effort$coverage <- factor(effort$coverage, levels = c('Good','Average','Bad','Not understood'))
  return(effort)
}

dir <- './Data'
effort <- get_effort(dir) %>% 
  mutate(survey = paste(.$site, .$atlas, sep='_')) %>% 
  select(survey, coverage) %>% 
  rbind(., data.frame(
    survey = paste(thresholds, 3, sep='_'),
    coverage = 'Good'
  ))

#### ENVIRONMENT ####
lulc_lookup <- c("0"="ocean", "11"="urban", "22"="cropland", "33"="pasture", "44"="forest", "55"="grass_shrub", "66"="other", "77"="water")

X <- read.csv(file.path(input, 'Data/data/1_preprocessing/X_environmental/X_Environmental.csv'), row.names=1) %>%
  rename_with(
    .cols = matches("^LULC_"),
    .fn = function(col) {
      lulc_code <- stringr::str_extract(col, "\\d+")
      paste0("perc_", lulc_lookup[lulc_code])
    }
  ) %>%
  mutate(perc_fresh_saltwater = perc_water + perc_ocean) %>%
  select(-perc_other, -perc_ocean, -perc_water) %>%
  mutate(
    dominant = factor(names(select(., starts_with("perc_")))[max.col(select(., starts_with("perc_")), ties.method = "first")])
  ) %>%
  filter(sub("_[123]$", "", rownames(.)) %in% thresholds) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(rownames(.) %in% effort$survey[effort$coverage == 'Good'])
```

```{r functions, include = F} 

Y_matrix <- Y
plot_title <- 'test'
getYsub <- function(Y_matrix, filter_type = "each", min_occs = 5, plot_title)  {
  
  # 1. Prepare data
  Y_long <- Y_matrix %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("site") %>%
    mutate(atlas = str_extract(site, "(?<=_)\\d$")) %>% 
    pivot_longer(-c(site, atlas), names_to = "species", values_to = "occ")
  
  # 2. Filter logic based on type ("each" vs "total")
  if (filter_type == "each") {
    to_remove <- Y_long %>%
      group_by(atlas, species) %>%
      summarise(n = sum(occ, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(n < min_occs) %>%
      pull(species) %>%
      unique()
  } else if (filter_type == "total") {
    to_remove <- Y_long %>%
      group_by(species) %>%
      summarise(total_occ = sum(occ, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(total_occ < min_occs) %>%
      pull(species)
  }
  
  # Subset matrix
  Y_sub <- Y_matrix[, !(colnames(Y_matrix) %in% to_remove), drop = FALSE]
  return(Y_sub)
# STI my birds 
}
```

```{r helper,include=F}
# --- HELPER: Calculate Stats ---
prep_atlas_data <- function(Y, X, sti_df) {
  # 1. Convert Y to long format
  Y_long <- as.data.frame(Y) %>%
    mutate(SiteID = rownames(Y)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -SiteID, names_to = "SPECIES", values_to = "Presence") %>%
    filter(Presence == 1) # We only care where they are present
  
  # 2. Add Environment data from X
  X_data <- as.data.frame(X) %>%
    mutate(SiteID = rownames(X),
           # Extract Atlas number from SiteID (e.g., AD90_1 -> Atlas 1)
           Atlas = str_extract(SiteID, "(?<=_)[0-9]+$"))
  
  # 3. Join everything together
  full_df <- Y_long %>%
    left_join(X_data, by = "SiteID") %>%
    left_join(sti_df %>% select(SPECIES, STI), by = "SPECIES")
  
  return(full_df)
}
# --- 1. CLEANED HELPER FUNCTION ---
```

```{r,fig.height=15,fig.width=10}
get_summary_stats <- function(data, X_full, n_species, mode) {
  
  # Species Stats (Now includes n_sites for occupancy)
  spec_stats <- data %>%
    group_by(SPECIES, Atlas) %>%
    summarise(
      median_temp = median(tmean_breeding, na.rm = TRUE),
      q25_temp = quantile(tmean_breeding, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q75_temp = quantile(tmean_breeding, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_sites = n(), # <--- NEW: Count of occupied sites
      STI = first(STI),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Filter for Top/Bottom species based on STI
  unique_specs <- spec_stats %>% 
    distinct(SPECIES, STI) %>% 
    arrange(STI)
  
  target_specs <- if(mode == "high") tail(unique_specs$SPECIES, n_species) else head(unique_specs$SPECIES, n_species)
  plot_df <- spec_stats %>% filter(SPECIES %in% target_specs)
  
  return(plot_df)
}

plot_atlas_comparison <- function(data, X_full, n_species = 100, mode = "high", plot_type = "segment", metric = "temperature") {
  
  # 1. Calculate Global Stats & Species List
  full_stats <- get_summary_stats(data, X_full, n_species, mode)
  
  # We need ALL species stats to find the community median for occupancy background
  if(metric == "occupancy") {
    all_stats <- get_summary_stats(data, X_full, n_species = 9999, mode = "high") 
  }
  
  # 2. Internal Helper: Calculate Limits per Atlas
  get_atlas_limits <- function(atlas_num) {
    if (metric == "temperature") {
      bg_vals <- X_full[str_detect(rownames(X_full), paste0("_", atlas_num)), "tmean_breeding"]
      spec_vals <- full_stats %>% filter(Atlas == as.character(atlas_num))
      all_vals <- c(bg_vals, spec_vals$q25_temp, spec_vals$q75_temp, spec_vals$median_temp)
    } else {
      # For occupancy, the range is determined by the site counts across all species
      all_vals <- all_stats %>% filter(Atlas == as.character(atlas_num)) %>% pull(n_sites)
    }
    return(range(all_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  
  # 3. Internal Helper: Header Boxplot
  make_header <- function(atlas_num, xlims) {
    # Custom titles for the periods
    title_text <- case_when(
      atlas_num == 1 ~ "1970s",
      atlas_num == 2 ~ "1990s",
      atlas_num == 3 ~ "2010s",
      TRUE ~ paste("Atlas", atlas_num)
    )
    
    if (metric == "temperature") {
      atlas_bg <- as.data.frame(X_full) %>%
        mutate(Atlas = str_extract(rownames(X_full), "(?<=_)[0-9]+$")) %>%
        filter(Atlas == as.character(atlas_num))
      
      p <- ggplot(atlas_bg, aes(x = tmean_breeding, y = 1))
    } else {
      atlas_bg <- all_stats %>% filter(Atlas == as.character(atlas_num))
      p <- ggplot(atlas_bg, aes(x = n_sites, y = 1))
    }
    
    p + geom_boxplot(fill = "grey90", color = "black", alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 0.5) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = xlims) +
      theme_void() +
      theme(plot.margin = margin(b = 2, t = 10, l = 5, r = 5),
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12)) +
      labs(title = title_text)
  }
  
  # 4. Internal Helper: Body Plot (The Switch)
  make_body <- function(atlas_num, xlims, show_y = FALSE) {
    atlas_data <- full_stats %>% filter(Atlas == as.character(atlas_num))
    
    if (metric == "temperature") {
      bg_med <- median(X_full[str_detect(rownames(X_full), paste0("_", atlas_num)), "tmean_breeding"], na.rm = TRUE)
      x_label <- "Temp (°C)"
    } else {
      bg_med <- median(all_stats %>% filter(Atlas == as.character(atlas_num)) %>% pull(n_sites), na.rm = TRUE)
      x_label <- "Number of Occupied Sites"
    }
    
    p <- ggplot(atlas_data, aes(y = reorder(SPECIES, STI))) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = bg_med, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.4)
    
    # Toggle Geometry
    if (metric == "occupancy") {
      # Occupancy forces a lollipop plot because there is no q25/q75 for a single count
      p <- p + geom_segment(aes(x = bg_med, xend = n_sites, color = STI), linewidth = 0.8) +
               geom_point(aes(x = n_sites, color = STI), size = 1.5)
    } else {
      if (plot_type == "lollipop") {
        p <- p + geom_segment(aes(x = bg_med, xend = median_temp, color = STI), linewidth = 0.8) +
                 geom_point(aes(x = median_temp, color = STI), size = 1.5)
      } else {
        p <- p + geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q25_temp, xmax = q75_temp, color = STI), linewidth = 1.2) +
                 geom_point(aes(x = median_temp, color = STI), size = 1, color = "white", alpha = 0.5)
      }
    }
    
    p <- p + scale_x_continuous(limits = xlims) +
      scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("blue4", "darkorchid", "red2")) +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(x = x_label, y = "") +
      theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            legend.position = "none",
            plot.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 5, l = 5, r = 5))
    
    if(!show_y) {
      p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
    } else {
      p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic", size = 6))
    }
    return(p)
  }
  
  # 5. Build Columns
  lims1 <- get_atlas_limits(1); col1 <- plot_grid(make_header(1, lims1), make_body(1, lims1, TRUE), ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.06, 0.94), align = "v")
  lims2 <- get_atlas_limits(2); col2 <- plot_grid(make_header(2, lims2), make_body(2, lims2, FALSE), ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.06, 0.94), align = "v")
  lims3 <- get_atlas_limits(3); col3 <- plot_grid(make_header(3, lims3), make_body(3, lims3, FALSE), ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.06, 0.94), align = "v")
  
  # 6. Final Stitch
  top_row <- plot_grid(col1, col2, col3, ncol = 3, rel_widths = c(1.4, 1, 1), align = "h")
  
  # Get legend from a temporary plot
  leg_plot <- make_body(1, lims1, TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") + labs(color = "Species Temperature Index (°C)")
  shared_legend <- get_legend(leg_plot)
  
  # Add cowplot-compatible main title
  main_title <- if(metric == "temperature") 'Species Occupied Breeding Season Temperatures' else 'Species Breeding Season Site Occupancy'
  title_gg <- ggdraw() + draw_label(main_title, fontface = 'bold', x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)
  
  return(plot_grid(title_gg, top_row, shared_legend, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.05, 1, 0.05)))
}
```

# Thermal deviations 
```{r}
plot_thermal_deviations <- function(data, X_full, n_species = 100, mode = "high") {
  
  # 1. Get the Stats
  full_stats <- get_summary_stats(data, X_full, n_species, mode)
  
  # 2. Calculate Atlas Medians to find the "Zero" point for each period
  bg_medians <- as.data.frame(X_full) %>%
    mutate(Atlas = str_extract(rownames(X_full), "(?<=_)[0-9]+$")) %>%
    group_by(Atlas) %>%
    summarise(atlas_med = median(tmean_breeding, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  # 3. Calculate Deviations
  dev_data <- full_stats %>%
    left_join(bg_medians, by = "Atlas") %>%
    mutate(deviation = median_temp - atlas_med)
  
  # 4. Create the Plot
  ggplot(dev_data, aes(x = deviation, y = reorder(SPECIES, STI), group = SPECIES)) +
    # Reference line at 0 (Species is exactly at the Atlas Median)
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    
    # Draw paths between Atlas points to show the "trajectory" of the shift
    geom_path(aes(color = STI), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm")), 
              alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.5) +
    
    # Points for each Atlas
    geom_point(aes(color = STI, shape = Atlas), size = 2) +
    
    scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("blue4", "darkorchid", "red2")) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = "Thermal Niche Tracking: Deviation from Atlas Median",
      subtitle = "Points further left are colder than the average available habitat.\nArrows show movement from Atlas 1 -> 2 -> 3.",
      x = "Deviation from Atlas Median (°C)",
      y = "",
      shape = "Atlas Period"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic", size = 7),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}
plot_thermal_reshuffle <- function(data, X_full, n_species = 50, mode = "high") {
  
  # 1. Get Stats and calculate Atlas Medians
  full_stats <- get_summary_stats(data, X_full, n_species, mode)
  
  bg_medians <- as.data.frame(X_full) %>%
    mutate(Atlas = str_extract(rownames(X_full), "(?<=_)[0-9]+$")) %>%
    group_by(Atlas) %>%
    summarise(atlas_med = median(tmean_breeding, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  # 2. Calculate Deviation and Rank within each Atlas
  reshuffle_data <- full_stats %>%
    left_join(bg_medians, by = "Atlas") %>%
    mutate(deviation = median_temp - atlas_med) %>%
    group_by(Atlas) %>%
    mutate(rank = rank(-deviation, ties.method = "first")) %>% # Rank 1 = Warmest relative to mean
    ungroup()

  # 3. Create the Plot
  ggplot(reshuffle_data, aes(x = Atlas, y = rank, group = SPECIES)) +
    # The "shuffling" lines
    geom_line(aes(color = STI), linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
    
    # Points at each Atlas node
    geom_point(aes(color = STI), size = 3) +
    
    # Species Labels on the Left (Atlas 1) and Right (Atlas 3)
    geom_text(data = filter(reshuffle_data, Atlas == "1"), 
              aes(label = SPECIES), hjust = 1.1, size = 2.5, face = "italic") +
    geom_text(data = filter(reshuffle_data, Atlas == "3"), 
              aes(label = SPECIES), hjust = -0.1, size = 2.5, face = "italic") +
    
    # Formatting
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = 1:n_species) + # Rank 1 at the top
    scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("blue4", "darkorchid", "red2")) +
    expand_limits(x = c(0.5, 3.5)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Thermal Reshuffling: Rank by Positive Deviation",
      subtitle = "Rank 1 = Seeking the warmest available habitat. Lines show changes in relative thermal position.",
      x = "Atlas Period",
      y = "Rank (Warmest -> Coldest seekers)",
      color = "STI"
    ) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)
    )
}
```

```{r}
plot_sti_adaptive_trends <- function(data, X_full, n_groups = 3, metric = "temperature") {
  
  all_stats <- get_summary_stats(data, X_full, n_species = 1000, mode = "high")
  
  all_stats <- all_stats %>% mutate(Group_ID = ntile(STI, n_groups))
  
  group_labels <- sapply(1:n_groups, function(i) {
    if(i == 1) return("Group 1 (cold)")
    if(i == n_groups) return(paste0("Group ", i, " (warm)"))
    return(paste0("Group ", i))
  })
  
  all_stats$STI_Group <- factor(all_stats$Group_ID, labels = group_labels)

  if (metric == "temperature") {
    bg_medians <- as.data.frame(X_full) %>%
      mutate(Atlas = str_extract(rownames(X_full), "(?<=_)[0-9]+$")) %>%
      group_by(Atlas) %>%
      summarise(atlas_med = median(tmean_breeding, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

    dev_data <- all_stats %>%
      left_join(bg_medians, by = "Atlas") %>%
      mutate(deviation = median_temp - atlas_med)
      
    y_label <- "Deviation from median breeding temperatures"
    plot_title <- paste("How is warming through time influencing relative warmth of sites that species breed in?")
    plot_sub <- "Species are grouped by thermal affinity (group 5 high = warm, group 1 low = cold)"
    
  } else if (metric == "occupancy") {
    bg_medians <- all_stats %>%
      group_by(Atlas) %>%
      summarise(atlas_med = median(n_sites, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

    dev_data <- all_stats %>%
      left_join(bg_medians, by = "Atlas") %>%
      mutate(deviation = n_sites - atlas_med)
      
    y_label <- "Deviation from median occupancy across the full species-set (per atlas)"
    plot_title <- paste("How is warming through time influencing species occupancy?")
    plot_sub <- "Species are grouped by thermal affinity (group 5 high = warm, group 1 low = cold)"
  }

  group_summary <- dev_data %>%
    group_by(STI_Group, Atlas) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_dev = mean(deviation, na.rm = TRUE),
      se_dev = sd(deviation, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
      n_species = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  my_custom_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue4", "darkorchid", "red2"))
  
  ggplot(group_summary, aes(x = Atlas, y = mean_dev, color = STI_Group, group = STI_Group)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_dev - se_dev, ymax = mean_dev + se_dev), 
                  width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = my_custom_palette(n_groups)) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
    scale_x_discrete(breaks = c("1", "2", "3"), labels = c("1970s", "1990s", "2010s")) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = plot_title, subtitle = plot_sub,
      x = "Atlas Period", y = y_label, color = "Species thermal index"
    ) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95")
    )
}
plot_sti_adaptive_trends(master_df,X,n_groups=5,metric = 'temperature')
```

# Bring effect sizes into this --> do changes in effect sizes follow expectations? 

```{r}
dir <- './HmscOutputs'
pattern <- '2026-02-10'
make_VP_effect_sizes <- function(dir,pattern){
  pattern2match <- pattern
  
  matching_folders <- list.dirs(dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = F)
  matching_folders <- matching_folders[grepl(pattern2match, basename(matching_folders))]
  model <- matching_folders[1]
  
  outputs <- lapply(matching_folders,function(model){
    # read objects
    MF <- readRDS(file.path(dir,
                            model,
                            'Results',
                            sprintf('%sMF.rds',
                                    model)))
    VP <- readRDS(file.path(dir,
                            model,
                            'Results',
                            sprintf('%sVP.rds',
                                    model)))
    effect_sizes <- read_excel(file.path(dir,
                                         model,
                                         'Results',
                                         sprintf('%sparameter_estimates_Beta_.xlsx',model)),
                               sheet = "Posterior mean")
    effect_sigs <- read_excel(file.path(dir,
                                        model,
                                        'Results',
                                        sprintf('%sparameter_estimates_Beta_.xlsx',model)),
                              sheet = "Pr(x>0)")
    
    load(file.path(dir,
                   model,
                   'Models/Fitted',
                   sprintf('HPC_samples_0250_thin_100_chains_4.Rdata')))
    m <- fitted_model$posteriors
    # get the atlas used
    X <- m$XData
    atlas <- unique(sapply(strsplit(rownames(X),'_'),'[',2))
    # get number of occurrences in that atlas
    if(!length(atlas)==1){
      stop()
    }
    occs <- data.frame(occs = colSums(m$Y,na.rm=T),
                       atlas = atlas)
    row.names(occs) <- colnames(m$Y)
    # get the trait date
    Tr <- m$TrData
    #transpose VP
    df <-VP$vals # get vals
    df <- as.data.frame(t(df)) # transpose into dataframe
    
    # merge VP with species info
    # 1. Prepare metrics and relative df first
    metrics <- data.frame(tjur = MF$TjurR2, auc = MF$AUC, row.names = m$spNames)
    df_rel <- metrics$tjur * df
    
    # 2. The main pipe, adding the scaled VPs 
    TrOccsTjurVP <- Tr %>%
      rownames_to_column("species") %>%
      inner_join(rownames_to_column(occs, "species"), by = "species") %>%
      inner_join(rownames_to_column(metrics, "species"), by = "species") %>%
      inner_join(rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(df_rel), "species"), by = "species") %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = c(tmean_year, prec_year, hh, `Random: site`,
                 starts_with("perc_")),   
        names_to = "environmental_variable",
        values_to = "VP_scaled_by_Tjur"
      )
    
    # 1. Pivot Effect Sizes to long format
    long_effects <- effect_sizes %>%
      select(-`(Intercept)`) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = -Species, names_to = "environmental_variable", values_to = "effect_size") %>%
      rename(species = Species)
    
    # 2. Pivot Significance to long format
    long_sigs <- effect_sigs %>%
      select(-`(Intercept)`) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = -Species, names_to = "environmental_variable", values_to = "sig_val") %>%
      rename(species = Species)
    
    # 3. Join, Mask, and Merge with your main data
    final_df <- long_effects %>%
      left_join(long_sigs, by = c("species", "environmental_variable")) %>%
      # Apply the mask: Keep only if sig <= 0.05 OR sig >= 0.95
      mutate(effect_size = ifelse(sig_val > 0.05 & sig_val < 0.95, NA, effect_size)) %>%
      select(-sig_val)
    # Join to your previous master table (assuming row names are Species)
    
    combined <- TrOccsTjurVP %>% 
      left_join(final_df,by=c("species","environmental_variable"))
    
    combined
    # adding effect sizes 
  })
  merged <- do.call(rbind,outputs)
  return(merged)
}
df <- make_VP_effect_sizes(dir,pattern)

# 1. Calculate the "Global Yardstick" parameters
# We use a separate temporary object to calculate the scaling factors
scaling_factors <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(effect_size)) %>%
  group_by(environmental_variable) %>%
  summarise(
    global_mean = mean(effect_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    global_sd = sd(effect_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

library(broom)
# 2. Join back to the original dataframe and calculate the score
df_final <- df %>%
  left_join(scaling_factors, by = "environmental_variable") %>%
  mutate(
    # Only calculates for rows where effect_size and global_sd exist
    std_effect_size = (effect_size - global_mean) / global_sd
  ) %>%
  mutate(std_effect_size = coalesce(std_effect_size, 0)) %>% 
  filter(environmental_variable == 'tmean_year' ) %>% 
  select(species, occs, atlas, std_effect_size)

# make any NAs 0 and only select temperature values 
head(df_final)

# get slopes for each estimate 
df_slopes <- df_final %>% 
   mutate(atlas = as.numeric(atlas)) %>% 
   group_by(species) %>% 
   # Run the model and tidy it
   do(tidy(lm(std_effect_size ~ atlas, data = .))) %>%
   # KEEP ONLY THE SLOPE ROW
   filter(term == "atlas") %>% 
   select(species, slope = estimate, p_value = p.value)

# merge with sti 
sti_estimate_slopes <- df_slopes %>% 
  left_join(sti %>% 
              rename(species = SPECIES),
            by = 'species'
              )
  
ggplot(data=sti_estimate_slopes,
       aes(x=slope,y=STI)) +
  geom_point()

# 1. Prepare data (Filter out NaNs and pick top/bottom species)
# 1. Define the number of groups

prep_thermal_slopes <- function(df, n_groups = 3) {
  # 1. Generate dynamic labels based on n_groups
  group_labels <- sapply(1:n_groups, function(i) {
    if (i == 1) return("Group 1 (Lowest STI)")
    if (i == n_groups) return(paste0("Group ", i, " (Highest STI)"))
    return(paste0("Group ", i))
  })
  
  # 2. Process the data
  df_prepped <- df %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(p_value)) %>%
    # Create the numeric bins
    mutate(Group_ID = ntile(STI, n_groups)) %>% 
    # Apply the dynamic labels
    mutate(Thermal_Range = factor(Group_ID, labels = group_labels)) %>%
    arrange(desc(slope))
    
  return(df_prepped)
}
plot_modular_slopes <- function(df, n_groups = 3, n_top_bottom = 25) {
  
  # Prepare the data
  processed_df <- prep_thermal_slopes(df, n_groups)
  
  # Slice for top and bottom species for readability
  plot_df <- processed_df %>%
    slice(c(1:n_top_bottom, (n() - (n_top_bottom - 1)):n()))
  
  # Generate colors dynamically: blue4 -> darkorchid -> red2
  group_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("blue4", "darkorchid", "red2"))(n_groups)
  
  # Create Plot
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = slope, y = reorder(ENGL.NAME, slope))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = slope, yend = ENGL.NAME, color = Thermal_Range), 
                 linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(color = Thermal_Range), size = 3) +
    # Significance circles
    geom_point(data = filter(plot_df, p_value < 0.05), 
               shape = 1, size = 4.5, color = "black", stroke = 0.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Species Slopes by Thermal Group (n =", n_groups, ")"),
      subtitle = paste("Top and bottom", n_top_bottom, "species shown. Circles = p < 0.05"),
      x = "Slope Value",
      y = "",
      color = "STI Rank"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7, face = "italic"),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
    )
}

plot_modular_slopes(sti_estimate_slopes, n_groups = 5,n_top_bottom = 100)

plot_thermal_slope_summary <- function(df, n_groups = 3) {
  
  # 1. Reuse the prep logic for consistency
  processed_df <- prep_thermal_slopes(df, n_groups)
  
  # 2. Generate colors
  group_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("blue4", "darkorchid", "red2"))(n_groups)
  
  # 3. Create the Plot
  ggplot(processed_df, aes(x = Thermal_Range, y = slope, fill = Thermal_Range)) +
    # Add a reference line at zero
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.4) +
    
    # Boxplot for the distribution summary
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +
    
    # Add "jittered" points so we can still see the individual species
    geom_jitter(aes(color = Thermal_Range), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
    scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = "Slope of temperature effect sizes by Thermal Group",
      x = "Thermal Guild",
      y = "Slope (Rate of Change)",
      fill = "STI Rank",
      color = "STI Rank"
    ) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none", # Legend is redundant because of x-axis labels
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1)
    )
}
plot_thermal_slope_summary(sti_estimate_slopes,n_groups = 5)
```
